import MumfordLib.SingularSmallCochainPrimitive
import MumfordLib.SingularSmallCochainsCircle
import MumfordLib.SingularSmallChainsAPI

/-!
# Vanishing of circle cohomology above degree one

The calculation on the two antipodal punctured-circle charts gives a
cohomologous representative vanishing on small chains. Subdivision supplies a
primitive for this representative, proving integral singular cohomology of the
circle is zero in every degree at least two.

This proves the higher-degree vanishing used in Mumford, Chapter I, Section 1,
p. 3.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory

namespace Mumford.Analytic

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Every integral singular circle cocycle of degree at least two has a primitive. -/
theorem singularCocycle_circle_exists_primitive {n : ℕ}
    (φ : singularCocycles (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 2)) :
    ∃ ψ : IntegralSingularCochain (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1),
      singularCoboundaryToCocycles (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1) ψ = φ := by
  let v : Circle := 1
  let U : Bool → Set (TopCat.of Circle) := fun b => if b then {v}ᶜ else {-v}ᶜ
  obtain ⟨hleft, hright, hcover⟩ := circle_antipodal_charts_open_cover v
  have hopen : ∀ b, IsOpen (U b) := by
    intro b
    cases b
    · exact hright
    · exact hleft
  have hU : ∀ x : TopCat.of Circle, ∃ b, x ∈ U b := by
    intro x
    have hx : x ∈ ({v}ᶜ ∪ {-v}ᶜ : Set Circle) := by
      rw [hcover]
      trivial
    rcases hx with hx | hx
    · exact ⟨true, hx⟩
    · exact ⟨false, hx⟩
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := singularCocycle_circle_exists_representative_zero_on_small v n φ
  have hsmall : (smallSingularChainInclusion (TopCat.of Circle) U).f (n + 2) ≫
      (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0 := by
    change simplicialCochainPullback
      (smallSingularSubcomplex (TopCat.of Circle) U).ι (n + 2)
      (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0
    have hA : smallSingularSubcomplex (TopCat.of Circle) U =
        singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ ⊔
          singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {-v}ᶜ :=
      smallSingularSubcomplex_two (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ {-v}ᶜ
    rw [hA]
    exact hψ
  have hcocycle : singularCochainCoboundary
      (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0 := by
    change singularCochainDifferential (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 2)
      (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0
    rw [map_sub]
    change singularCochainCoboundary φ.1 -
      singularCochainCoboundary (singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0
    have hφ : singularCochainCoboundary φ.1 = 0 := φ.2
    rw [hφ, singularCochainCoboundary_squared, sub_self]
  obtain ⟨θ, hθ⟩ := singularCocycle_exists_primitive_of_zero_on_small U hopen hU
    (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) hcocycle hsmall
  refine ⟨ψ + θ, Subtype.ext ?_⟩
  change singularCochainDifferential (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1) (ψ + θ) = φ.1
  rw [map_add]
  change singularCochainCoboundary ψ + singularCochainCoboundary θ = φ.1
  rw [hθ]
  abel

/-- Integral singular cohomology of the circle vanishes in degree at least two. -/
theorem integralSingularCohomology_circle_eq_zero {n : ℕ}
    (c : IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 2)) : c = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨φ, rfl⟩ :=
    singularPositiveCohomologyClass_surjective (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1) c
  exact (singularPositiveCohomologyClass_eq_zero_iff (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1) φ).mpr
    (singularCocycle_circle_exists_primitive φ)

/-- The higher integral singular cohomology groups of the circle are trivial. -/
theorem integralSingularCohomology_circle_subsingleton (n : ℕ) :
    Subsingleton (IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 2)) := by
  refine ⟨fun c d => ?_⟩
  rw [integralSingularCohomology_circle_eq_zero c,
    integralSingularCohomology_circle_eq_zero d]

end Mumford.Analytic
